newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares chase Dow to record levels.
newsitem.headline: German shares chase Dow to record levels.

text.p: The German share market ended bourse trade on Tuesday at a record closing high, powered ahead by record overnight gains in the U.S. and Japan and well-received results from top companies.
After setting a new session high of 3,584.56 points in earlx trade, the blue chip DAX index pared its gains to close at 3,568.28, up 39.50 points, or 1.12 percent.

Modest trading volumes and a smattering of profit-taking, however, meant shares lost the early momentum which pushed the IBIS DAX of electronic trade over 3,600 points for the first time ever in pre-bourse dealings.
Nonetheless, the mood on the floor was optimistic.
"All the news has been positive today," said a Frankfurt dealer. "Wall Street was good, the Nikkei was better and we are simply keeping up."
Heading the field was diversified energy group Veba, boosted by a first quarter earnings report that dealers said was significatly above expectations.
Sportswear firm Adidas was also among the morning's outperformers after reporting a 33 percent rise in first quarter net profit, although its advance ebbed as trading continued.
Veba's shares ended floor trading up 3.45 marks at 93.55.
Veba said its first quarter net profit after minorities rose seven percent to 486 million marks while pre-tax profit rose 6.8 percent to 1.08 billion marks.
Adidas closed up 1.90 marks at 182.40 marks in bourse trade, off an early high of 185.50 marks.

Hoechst AG shares climbed 1.73 marks to 68.08 as management board chairman Juergen Dormann told the group's annual meeting that operating profit is expected to show an increase on an adjusted basis in 1997.
